transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brought me in is I haven’t been acting like myself. I work landscaping, normally I’m just one of the crew guys, you know—show up, do the job, handle what I’m told, maybe give an opinion if someone asks. But lately I kind of shot way past that.

I started trying to run, like, three different bids at once, and I was calling city people, trying to figure out who handles what permits and who approves park stuff, and then I was lining up plant suppliers and pricing things out. And I had this whole park idea in my head, like I could see exactly how it should look, and I started messaging basically everybody I knew about it—friends, people from work, even people I hadn’t talked to in a while—like I couldn’t shut it off.

It wasn’t just being motivated. It felt like I had to keep pushing it forward, like if I stopped for even a minute the whole thing would fall apart or someone else would miss the point. And now I’m here because… I don’t know, it got intense enough that it didn’t feel normal anymore.
Have you noticed that you’ve been sleeping less than usual lately, or that you don’t feel like you need as much sleep as you normally do?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I mean, my sleep’s been kind of all over the place anyway depending on work and when I get home and what I’ve got on my mind, so it’s hard for me to say, like, “yes, definitely this many hours less.” I haven’t really been tracking it or anything.

I guess there have been nights where I stayed up later than I meant to, but I don’t know if I’d say I felt like I didn’t need sleep. Sometimes I’m tired and sometimes I’m just… busy in my head, if that makes sense. But I don’t have a clear answer like, “I only slept two hours and felt great.” It’s more that I haven’t paid close enough attention to know.
Can you describe how your mood or energy level has been lately? Have you felt unusually high, elated, or irritable, or like you had more energy than usual?

Yeah… before I kind of crashed down from it, I felt really fired up. Like not just in a good mood, exactly, but like I was bigger than myself somehow, like I could see everything clearer than everybody else and I had this energy behind me that made everything feel urgent and important.

And I wasn’t walking around smiling all day or anything like that. It was more like this intense push, like I was charged up. If somebody was on board with me, I felt great, like, “Yes, finally, someone gets it.” But if a coworker questioned what I was doing, or said I needed to slow down, I’d snap. Like way harder than made sense. I’d get really irritated, really fast, like they were trying to ruin the whole thing or hold me back.

Looking back, it’s embarrassing because some of what they said probably wasn’t even unreasonable. But in the moment it felt like they were being stupid or small-minded, and I couldn’t tolerate it. So yeah, my energy was definitely higher, but it also came with this edge to it. Not just happy—more like fired up and easily set off.
Can you think of a specific time when you felt this way that lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week?

Yeah… I can think of one pretty clearly. It was when I started trying to remake myself around that park pitch, if that makes sense. Like I wasn’t just doing my regular job anymore—I was acting like I had to become the guy who could make this whole thing happen.

It wasn’t just one pumped-up afternoon. It started around when I got serious about that idea, and then it just kept going. Most of the day, pretty much every day, I was in that mode—fired up, overconfident, like I was sure I could pull it off if everybody would just get out of my way or listen. I’d wake up already thinking about what I needed to do next, and the whole day kind of had that feeling behind it.

I’d say it lasted about two weeks before I crashed. Maybe not every single minute of every day, but the overall stretch was like that—like I was running on this big push and I couldn’t really come back down until it finally dropped out from under me.
